module: D10-13 Trade Policy／Export Controls／Sanctions Supply-chain Transmission貿易政策出口管制制裁供應鏈傳導

sources.use: Current EAR end-use/end-user and semiconductor manufacturing controls.
Geoeconomic fragmentation and trade-restriction transmission context.

mechanisms: Export controls can alter who may buy, fabricate, package, service or expand controlled technology; impact depends on exact item/end-use/end-user and jurisdiction scope.
Rules can redirect demand/capacity toward compliant suppliers or locations, but can also reduce addressable market and increase compliance cost.
Policy uncertainty itself can cause pre-buying, inventory buffering or order rerouting before economic effects are realized.
falsification: Official announcement is not equivalent to effective enforcement; the 2025 AI Diffusion Rule was issued with a future compliance date and then rescinded before enforcement.
A rule can contain exemptions, license exceptions, grandfathering or transition periods that materially alter issuer exposure.
A sector may have both beneficiaries and victims; domestic or allied suppliers may gain substitution demand while losing customers or facing higher compliance costs.
Company exposure cannot be inferred from headquarters nationality alone; product, customer, manufacturing location and EAR jurisdiction matter.
Market reaction to a policy headline is not evidence of realized revenue/capacity impact.

pitContract.revisionRule: Every amendment/rescission is a new policy vintage; prior state remains immutable.
pitContract.outcomeFirewall: No stock return or realized revenue outcome until event and issuer exposure are frozen.

redundancyControls: News/event timing belongs to D17/D11; D10-13 owns physical/economic supply-chain transmission.
Do not duplicate D10-08 shortage state; policy is a cause/context that may or may not create shortage.
Do not duplicate D13 macro trade-regime variables as issuer-specific exposure.
reasonNoL3: A Taiwan issuer-level effective-dated policy-exposure dataset has not yet been frozen across controlled products, destinations, end-users and transition clocks.
